h: Sculpture, Gardens and a Spot of Racing
p: Harlow's new-town story is a fascinating one. It was designed after the Second World War by the architect Sir Frederick Gibberd, and his own home and garden, The Gibberd Garden, is open to visitors on selected days. It's a quirky, peaceful place full of sculptures and pools, and a real contrast to the noise and speed of an indoor kart track.

If you prefer something wilder, Epping Forest isn't far to the south-west, with miles of ancient woodland to explore. It's ideal if your group fancies stretching its legs after an hour or so of sitting in a kart.

On the track, the best tip for beginners is to stay relaxed. Grip the wheel firmly but not tightly, look ahead and let the kart flow through the bends rather than wrestling it. You'll be quicker and less worn out.
Harlow Town station has fast trains to London Liverpool Street and Cambridge.

If you're organising a group, it pays to book well ahead and to tell everyone the meeting time rather than the race time, so you've got a buffer for late arrivals. Karting sessions run to a schedule, so one straggler can mean the whole group misses out. And make sure everyone's got sensible shoes on, because trainers or flat boots are what you want, not sandals.
